stops.title: Kirchhoff's laws of electrical networks
stops.inShort: KCL (Junction law): ∑I = 0 (conservation of charge). KVL (Loop law): ∑IR + ∑E = 0 around any closed loop (conservation of energy).

stops.title: Wheatstone bridge & Metre bridge
stops.inShort: Balanced Wheatstone bridge: P/Q = R/S (no current through galvanometer). Metre bridge uses a 1 m uniform wire to find unknown resistance X = R (l_X / l_R).

stops.title: Potentiometer principle & applications
stops.inShort: Potential drop across uniform wire carrying steady current is proportional to length: V = K l (K = potential gradient). Used to compare emfs (E₁/E₂ = l₁/l₂) and find internal resistance r = R(l₁/l₂ − 1). Draws zero current at null point.

stops.title: Galvanometer as ammeter & voltmeter
stops.inShort: To convert MCG (resistance G, full-scale I_g) into ammeter of range I: connect low shunt S = I_g G / (I − I_g) in parallel. To convert into voltmeter of range V: connect high resistance X = V/I_g − G in series.

items.s: Metre bridge: X = R · l_X / (100 − l_X).

items.f: S = I_g G / (I − I_g),  X = (V / I_g) − G

board.text: Which of the following equations gives correct expression for the internal resistance of a cell by using potentiometer?
State the advantages of a potentiometer over a voltmeter.
board.answer:
1. Potentiometer is more sensitive than a voltmeter and can measure very small potential differences accurately.
2. At the null point, potentiometer draws no current from the cell, so it measures the true emf (whereas a voltmeter draws current and measures terminal p.d.).
3. Accuracy can be increased simply by increasing the length of the wire.

points.text: Draws zero current at null point (measures true emf)

board.text: A galvanometer has a resistance of 50 Ω and a current of 2 mA is needed for its full scale deflection. Calculate resistance required to convert it into (i) an ammeter of 0.5 A range and (ii) a voltmeter of 10 V range.
board.answer:
Given: G = 50 Ω, I_g = 2 mA = 2 × 10⁻³ A.
(i) Ammeter (I = 0.5 A): S = I_g G / (I − I_g) = (2 × 10⁻³ × 50) / (0.5 − 0.002) = 0.1 / 0.498 ≈ 0.2008 Ω (connected in parallel).
(ii) Voltmeter (V = 10 V): X = V/I_g − G = (10 / 2×10⁻³) − 50 = 5000 − 50 = 4950 Ω (connected in series).

points.text: Shunt S = I_g G/(I − I_g) = 0.201 Ω in parallel
Series resistance X = V/I_g − G = 4950 Ω in series

board.text: How will you convert a moving coil galvanometer into an ammeter?
board.answer:
A moving coil galvanometer is converted into an ammeter of range I by connecting a very small resistance called shunt (S) in parallel with the galvanometer coil.
Since G and S are in parallel, I_g G = (I − I_g) S ⇒ S = I_g G / (I − I_g).

board.text: Obtain the balancing condition for a Wheatstone bridge using Kirchhoff's laws.
board.answer:
Four resistors P, Q, R, S form a bridge ABCD with galvanometer G between B and D.
At balance, I_g = 0, so I₁ = I₃ and I₂ = I₄.
Applying KVL to loop ABDA: −I₁P + I₂R = 0 ⇒ I₁P = I₂R.
Applying KVL to loop BCDB: −I₁Q + I₂S = 0 ⇒ I₁Q = I₂S.
Dividing the two equations: P/Q = R/S.
